name: Lucidspark
tagline: Collaborative whiteboards for brainstorming, planning, and workshops

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 3 editable Lucidspark boards, unlimited shapes, 25 MB total Lucid storage, Lucid AI and basic Visual Activities

tiers.name: Individual
tiers.limits: Unlimited editable Lucidspark boards; 1 GB storage; premium Visual Activities
tiers.notes: The official current guide publishes $9 but not an unambiguous annual effective rate.

tiers.name: Team
tiers.limits: Unlimited editable boards; 1 GB storage per user; guest contributors, developer platform, custom templates and advanced collaboration
tiers.notes: The official current guide publishes $10 per user but not an unambiguous annual effective rate.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Lucid Visual Collaboration Suite, 5 GB storage per user, SAML/SCIM, central administration, security and governance
tiers.notes: Custom quote; Enterprise bundles Lucidspark with Lucidchart.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 3 editable Lucidspark boards, unlimited shapes and 25 MB total storage; basic Visual Activities and Lucid AI
pricing.billingTerms: free + recurring Individual/Team subscriptions and custom Enterprise; accessible first-party pages published $9 and $10 monthly figures but not verifiable annual equivalents
pricing.hiddenCosts: A Lucidspark-only Team license does not let the user create or edit Lucidchart documents; both products require separate Team licenses unless buying the Enterprise Suite; Accelerators and other enterprise add-ons are separate

verdictSummary: The visible whiteboarding loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. Lucidspark earns its keep through interaction polish, collaboration, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a browser-based whiteboarding editor with drag, resize, connect, keyboard shortcuts, autosave, and SVG or PNG export.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
whyPeopleStillPay: Lucidspark: The shapes are easy; customers pay for low-friction editing, reliable exports, collaboration, and a canvas that never fights them.
ongoingBurden: Own geometry, selection behavior, undo, clipboard interoperability, export fidelity, accessibility, and browser performance.

priorArt.name: Excalidraw
priorArt.desc: Open-source diagram canvas with an approachable interaction model.

alternatives.name: AFFiNE
alternatives.desc: Collaborative whiteboards tied to docs, databases, and planning views; broader than Lucidspark, more infrastructure if self-hosted.

facts.install: Hosted signup or desktop app; Docker Compose for self-hosting
facts.engines: Self-hosted AFFiNE AI can be configured with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, and FAL credentials
facts.dataFormat: Local-first clients keep workspace data locally and sync to AFFiNE Cloud or the operator's server; self-hosting uses PostgreSQL, Redis, and persistent blob storage
facts.gapVsPaid: AFFiNE offers a broad workspace but has a smaller facilitation toolkit, template library, timer and voting workflow, and integration ecosystem than Lucidspark.
facts.setupBlocker: The hosted/desktop app installs cleanly; self-hosting is a multi-service Docker deployment that needs a domain, TLS, secrets, storage, backups, and AI-provider keys for AI features

alternatives.name: CryptPad
alternatives.desc: Persistent encrypted whiteboards inside a shared drive with permissions and team folders; visually plain, operationally serious.

facts.install: Use a public CryptPad instance, or self-host the Node.js service behind a reverse proxy
facts.dataFormat: Documents are encrypted in the browser before upload; the server stores encrypted document files, blobs, and account pin metadata on its filesystem and cannot read document content
facts.gapVsPaid: Its whiteboard lacks Lucidspark's workshop templates, voting, timers, facilitation controls, breakout workflows, and polished participant experience.
facts.setupBlocker: Public hosting is immediate; self-hosting requires two domains or subdomains, HTTPS, strict security headers, Node.js configuration, persistent storage, and careful upgrades/backups

alternatives.name: Excalidraw
alternatives.desc: Fast multiplayer whiteboards, libraries, links, exports, and workshop-friendly sketching; fewer facilitation widgets, much less account bureaucracy.

facts.install: Open the hosted web app/PWA, or deploy the static app and optional collaboration server
facts.dataFormat: Solo drawings are stored in browser storage or explicit .excalidraw JSON files; exports include PNG and SVG; multiplayer room data is end-to-end encrypted and the decryption key is carried in the share URL
facts.gapVsPaid: Excalidraw is faster for sketching but omits many structured facilitation features such as advanced voting, timed activities, and enterprise workshop controls.
facts.setupBlocker: None for the hosted app; the trade-off appears later because durable workspace organization, centralized team administration, and managed version history are deliberately minimal

alternatives.name: tldraw
alternatives.desc: A frictionless hosted multiplayer canvas for brainstorming and planning; templates and enterprise workshop controls are sparse.

facts.install: Open tldraw.com in a browser; no account is required for a quick canvas
facts.dataFormat: Hosted shared canvases live in tldraw's cloud; local/offline documents use browser IndexedDB, and snapshots or .tldr JSON files can be exported
facts.gapVsPaid: tldraw's instant canvas has sparse workshop templates, facilitation widgets, integrations, and administrator controls compared with Lucidspark.

alternatives.name: WBO
alternatives.desc: The basic communal whiteboard that keeps working: persistent rooms, live cursors, free hosting, and almost no workshop theatre.

facts.install: Use the free hosted instance, or run the Docker image/Node.js server
facts.dataFormat: Boards are persisted as JSON files in the server's data directory; a Docker deployment must mount that directory, while public-hosted boards live on the operator's server
facts.gapVsPaid: WBO is a bare communal canvas without Lucidspark's templates, voting, timers, structured activities, integrations, or enterprise controls.
facts.setupBlocker: None for the public instance; self-hosting needs Docker or Node.js, a persistent writable volume with the expected user ownership, backups, and a public URL/TLS

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of Lucidspark is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for Lucidspark, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: React + TypeScript + Vite + IndexedDB.
Primary job: Build a browser-based whiteboarding editor with drag, resize, connect, keyboard shortcuts, autosave, and SVG or PNG export.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: high-fidelity import and export; presentation and enterprise controls; multiplayer cursors and comments.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
